extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, patent examiners, and students of patent practice
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing (1) how amendments to patent applications must relate to the original application and may be presented, and (2) how appeals from examiner decisions are classified, taken, and adjudicated through the Patent Office and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment subordinate to original application
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment, however extensive in substance or complete in form, must always be subordinate to, and connected with the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two distinct applications cannot qualify or support each other. A later application describing the same invention as an earlier one is not regarded as an amendment to the earlier; the earlier stands unaffected and may be amended and allowed without reference to the later. An amendment of one portion does not always change the rest except insofar as construing the whole together modifies the meaning of unaltered portions. A Claim may be amended without affecting the Description, or the Description without influencing the Claims, or the drawings/model without revising the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of cancelled claims must be separate amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a cancelled Claim is to be restored by amendment it must be done as a separate amendment, not by merely erasing the cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Erasing a prior cancellation is not a sufficient method to restore a cancelled claim (see Ex parte Mumler (1888)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended claims require applicant's signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended Claims may be inserted into an application by the attorney only with the signature of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney has no right to substitute a clean draft of a specification (or claims) signed and sworn to by the attorney alone; if done it must be erased (see Sheridan v. Latos (1883)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Later application by same inventor is independent
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application, by whomsoever filed, is regarded as that of an independent inventor and is in no manner affected by any other; a later application by the same inventor neither amends nor abandons the former.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A later application which describes but did not claim an invention in a still-pending former application cannot be treated as an amendment of the former. Where two applications describe the same invention but only one claims it, the patent may issue on the latter without affecting the earlier application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments offered to avoid references must point out novelty and avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: In offering an amendment for the purpose of removing any of the grounds on which an application has been rejected by the examiner, the applicant must point out all the patentable novelty which he thinks the case presents in view of the state of the art, as disclosed by the references cited or objections made, and must show how his amendment avoids such references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process may be repeated if the examiner produces new references or arguments. The applicant should explain how the amendment distinguishes over cited references; failure to do so risks further rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendments after final rejection without good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: After the final rejection of all the Claims no amendments are allowable, unless good cause is shown for permitting them, and satisfactory reasons are given for the delay in their presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the refusal of the examiner to allow such amendments an appeal lies to the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must examine amended application as original and communicate reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the filing of any amendment to meet the references and objections of the examiner, it is his duty to examine the case presented by the amended application in the same manner as if it were an original application, and if he rejects it to communicate his rejection with its reasons to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant may reply by argument or further amendment. After a second rejection of claims as originally filed, or if amended in substance, of the amended claims, the right of the applicant to a hearing before the examiner ceases and further action must be by appeal to the examiners-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct classification of appeals: form vs substance
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals in uncontested cases are based either upon the decisions of the examiner as to some matter of form, or upon his decision as to some matter of substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appeal upon a question of form lies to the Commissioner in person; an appeal upon a question of substance lies to the examiners-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — matter of form
rubrics_metrics.description: A matter of form is one that relates to the fitness of the application for an examination on its merits, or involves merely some rule of Office practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: joinder questions, claim intelligibility, whether a claim is functional (these are treated as matters of form in various cases). Appeals on matters of Office practice are appealable only to the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — matter of substance
rubrics_metrics.description: A matter of substance is one that pertains to the patentability of the invention as described and claimed in the application, or to the right of the inventor to a patent upon the application as presented by him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: whether a combination is a true combination or a mere aggregation; whether claims cover operative constructions; whether the invention is practicable, new, or useful; whether it has been abandoned to the public; whether an amendment departs from the original application — all are questions of substance and appeal lies to the examiners-in-chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedure for matters of form to Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal to the Commissioner from an adverse decision of an examiner upon a matter of form is taken by a written petition setting up the decision complained of and the reasons for the appeal, signed by the applicant or his attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must file a written statement disclosing grounds of his decision; upon hearing (oral or written) the Commissioner may affirm, reverse, or modify the examiner's action. This decision is final and can be reviewed or reconsidered only by the Commissioner himself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedure for matters of substance to examiners-in-chief
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal to the examiners-in-chief from an adverse decision of an examiner upon a matter of substance can be taken only after an original or amended claim has been twice rejected by the examiner and after all claims have been passed upon and all questions of form conclusively settled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeal is instituted by a written petition signed by applicant or authorized attorney setting forth the points and reasons. The examiner must furnish a written statement of grounds and copies of rejected claims and references. The appellant must file a brief of authorities and, if desired, indicate request for oral hearing; otherwise the case will be decided on the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners-in-chief limited to points of appeal but may raise new grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiners-in-chief can affirm or reverse the decision of the examiner only upon the points on which the appeal is taken; but if they discover any apparent grounds not involved in the appeal for granting or refusing letters-patent, they must annex a written statement of these grounds with recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those new grounds must then be considered by the examiner; from his adverse decision on those questions another appeal lies to the examiners-in-chief (substance) or to the Commissioner (form) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from examiners-in-chief to Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: From an adverse decision of the examiners-in-chief the applicant may appeal to the Commissioner in person by written petition specifying the judgment complained of and reasons of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner, in revising their decision, may discover apparent grounds not presented by the appeal and may give notice and remand the case to the examiner for his consideration. The Commissioner acts in a judicial capacity as a court of appellate jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal from Commissioner to Supreme Court (District of Columbia)
rubrics_metrics.description: From an adverse decision of the Commissioner on an appeal from the examiners-in-chief in ex parte cases a further appeal may be had to the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia by written petition with certified copies of the Patent Office record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appellant must give immediate written notice and file a statement of reasons constituting a full brief. The court confines itself to points set forth in the reasons of appeal and, after judgment, returns a certificate of its proceedings to be entered of record in the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable remedy after final rejection (bill in equity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Supreme Court of the District of Columbia decides against the applicant on appeal, he may pursue his remedy by bill in equity in the Circuit Court of the District, provided he has exhausted remedies by appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the bill must be served on the Commissioner. Jurisdiction and proper parties (e.g., opposing patentees, transferees) must be observed. The remedy applies where the Commissioner or Court has decided to reject an application on its merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal scope limited to issues within jurisdiction and on the record
rubrics_metrics.description: Only questions that were properly within the jurisdiction of the inferior tribunal can be presented on appeal; the appeal is limited to the issues apparent on the record and brings up only the particular adjudications complained of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions affecting matters not within the cognizance of the Patent Office (e.g., matters of title) are not reviewable. An appeal raising no issue will be dismissed. The presumption on appeal is in favor of the decision appealed from.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of new evidence during appeal requires remand
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidence is admitted during an appeal to support the applicant's claims against references or to vary factual issues concerning patentability, the whole case must be remanded to the examiner so that he may pass upon it in its new condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the examiner's primary fact-finding role and ensures issues of fact are first resolved at the Office level before final appellate adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: No appeal from judgments wholly in favor or until officially rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: No appeal lies from a judgment wholly in favor of the appellant, nor from any judgment until it has been duly rendered in the required official form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decisions below must be in proper official form to be appealable; judgments must be explicit so the subject of the appeal can be clearly distinguished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interlocutory appeal practice: examiner must act twice before Commissioner review
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the rule concerning interlocutory appeals, the principal examiner must act twice before review by the Commissioner is entertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlocutory appeals to the Commissioner are really petitions for orders; where the examiner refuses to reconsider after two acts, further review may be sought by appropriate appeal procedures (see Ex parte Bennett (1886) and related cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of appeals and effect on third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejected applicant must appeal within a reasonable time or he will not be permitted to stand in the way of other applicants; taking an appeal from the rejection of one claim forfeits no rights as to other claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays in prosecuting applications or suing in equity may be inquired into; unreasonable delay can bar relief or affect equities between competing applicants.
